account: Millie Houlton, a 22-year-old final-year events and business management student at York St John University, received a £60 parking notice from York City Council. It was for parking on her own street, where she holds a permit. Busy with coursework, she was tempted to pay. She typed into ChatGPT “please help me write a letter to the council, they gave me a parking ticket”. She gave the location, reference number and circumstances. The letter came back in minutes. Within days the council told her that the appeal was accepted and the fine withdrawn. The BBC first published the story on 30 March 2023, and ITV News and the Yorkshire Post reported it on 31 March 2023. She also shared it on TikTok. Fox News retold the BBC report on 2 April 2023. No source gives the date of the ticket or of the council's reply. About a month before the BBC report, the RAC reported that Shaun Bosley of Brighton had used ChatGPT to get an NCP fine at Gatwick Airport cut from £100 to £15.

ai_role.statement: ChatGPT drafted the appeal from the facts the student entered. The ground for withdrawal was her valid permit, which a human-written appeal could also have stated. The system's contribution was overcoming the effort barrier. She said she would otherwise have paid rather than spend time on a response. The council's reasoning has not been published, so the letter's causal weight is inferred, not documented.

fields.title: York student has a £60 parking fine withdrawn after sending an appeal letter drafted by ChatGPT

fields.account: Millie Houlton, a 22-year-old final-year events and business management student at York St John University, received a £60 parking notice from York City Council. It was for parking on her own street, where she holds a permit. Busy with coursework, she was tempted to pay. She typed into ChatGPT “please help me write a letter to the council, they gave me a parking ticket”. She gave the location, reference number and circumstances. The letter came back in minutes. Within days the council told her that the appeal was accepted and the fine withdrawn. The BBC first published the story on 30 March 2023, and ITV News and the Yorkshire Post reported it on 31 March 2023. She also shared it on TikTok. Fox News retold the BBC report on 2 April 2023. No source gives the date of the ticket or of the council's reply. About a month before the BBC report, the RAC reported that Shaun Bosley of Brighton had used ChatGPT to get an NCP fine at Gatwick Airport cut from £100 to £15.

echoes.setting: Gatwick Airport, England: Shaun Bosley of Brighton used ChatGPT to appeal an NCP drop-off fine, which was cut from £100 to £15

must_hold: The facts entered are true and the appellant checks the draft before sending. The model can produce plausible but incorrect text, as the BBC noted OpenAI admits.
The authority judges the appeal on its merits, so the outcome rests on the permit, not on prose quality.
produced_by: The appellant had a genuine ground (a valid residents' permit) and the specific facts to hand: location, date, reference number and circumstances.
The appeal channel accepted a written letter, so a well-formed draft was the whole task.
The user already used ChatGPT for work emails and so trusted it enough to try it rather than pay.

purpose: ChatGPT is a general-purpose conversational assistant built to answer questions and draft text on request. Writing a formal appeal letter from the user's facts falls within that purpose.

ratings.reason: One identifiable person avoided a £60 fine that she considered wrongly issued. She also saved the time of drafting an appeal, which she said that she found hard to articulate.

revisions.change: Record drafted from the OECD Monitor entry and the cited sources. The Monitor's listed sources are Macedonian-language reposts; the record is built on the BBC, ITV News, Yorkshire Post and Fox News originals. The BBC page displays 31 March 2023 while its metadata timestamp is 2023–03–30T16:21Z; the dates of the ticket and of the withdrawal letter are not reported, so the date observed is the reporting date. The Monitor's “hazard” label is dropped: the attached rationale concerns a different story (expert warnings about AI).
Benefit type set to Reduced Task Time under Trustible's full taxonomy of 23 types; it was Improved Accessibility among the six first used.
Added the value as stated from the cited sources.
Country of the developer and the deployer added from the organization's own site or a registry.
Rewrote the account, the purpose, the replication conditions and the statement of the system's part in shorter sentences, with abbreviations expanded; facts, figures and quotations unchanged.
Linked a comparable incident in the AI Incident Database (incident 709).
Dated the case to 30 March 2023 (source published); recorded what the benefit is measured against; recorded one other attempt to repeat the benefit.
Edited the headline, account of events, purpose for accuracy and clarity; revised the depth ratings; restated earlier revision notes.

summary: Millie Houlton, 22, asked ChatGPT to draft an appeal against a wrongly issued £60 parking fine; York City Council withdrew it.
taxonomy_note: The good is a wrongly issued 60-pound fine withdrawn, and the type names the minutes-long drafting of the appeal that produced it.
